Why LLM reinforcement learning breaks on robots, and how the frontier is fixing it

Why is reinforcement learning on robots so much harder than on language models, and why can't we reuse the LLM recipe? An LLM picks from a finite menu of tokens, so it gets the exact probability of each answer for free. A robot outputs continuous actions from a flow policy, which gives classical RL neither that probability nor a stable gradient through the critic. This review explains those constraints and how RECAP, π0.7, GVC, DSRL and QF3 work around them, and it ends with possible future directions.

Do you need a human body to use human data?

Figure AI says a humanoid can learn from human video because it is shaped like us. About 30 papers with measured results say human video also trains grippers and wheeled robots, that mismatch breaks transfer, and that the body decides what a robot can reach. A companion to Three robot bets, with a pinned blackboard.
